known.title: A new plan-cli test pins two sentences of the plan contract, but the plan-lifecycle contract-sync rule says that no test pins skill prose.
known.summary: The new test on scripts/tests/plan-cli/reviews.test.mjs:121-132 reads plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/references/plan-contract.md. It asserts two contract sentences with assert.match: 'indented by at most three spaces) that names the comment's kind.' and 'A quoted or list-item heading is prose and starts no block.' (plan-contract.md:191-193). Only this test uses the node:fs import on reviews.test.mjs:2. The test checks no helper behavior. The parser cases on reviews.test.mjs:93-116 already test the heading rule. The node that governs plan-contract.md has this contract-sync rule: '`plan-manager/references/plan-contract.md` is canonical.' (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/AGENTS.md:66) and '`scripts/tests/plan-cli.mjs` exercises the helper's behavior; no test pins skill prose.' (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/AGENTS.md:72-73). reviews.test.mjs is a case file of that suite: 'The live plan author suite is the set of plan-CLI case files in `scripts/tests/plan-cli/`. The `scripts/tests/plan-cli.mjs` entry runs them' (scripts/AGENTS.md:27-29). Scenario: a later edit rewords the rule without a change of meaning, for example 'indented by at most three spaces' becomes 'with at most three spaces of indentation'. Then node scripts/tests/plan-cli.mjs fails, and the gate blocks a prose-only change of the contract. Fix: remove the test and the node:fs import.

known.title: The contract still says that the helper ignores blockquote and list markers on each line, but the helper now reads a block heading from the raw line.
known.summary: plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/references/plan-contract.md:196-197 says: 'On each line, the helper ignores Markdown emphasis (`*`, `_`), code marks, blockquote markers, and list markers.' The change keeps this sentence. But the new rule four lines above says: 'A quoted or list-item heading is prose and starts no block.' (plan-contract.md:192-193). The code now tests the raw line for a block heading: parseReviewComment gives rawLines[index] to blockHeadingKind (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs:771-775). The comment on plan.mjs:751-752 says that 'only the title after the `#` markers is read through emphasis and code marks'. The plan keeps the marker reading only for kinds and verdict lines (plan line 8: 'Kinds and verdict lines keep the #49 reading through emphasis, code marks, quotes, and list markers.'; plan line 29: 'Keep `reviewText()` for the first line, the verdict lines, and the severity scan'). So the sentence restates the old behavior, and the canonical contract contradicts itself. Scenario: an agent checks how the helper reads the line '> ### Code review round 1' in a delta block. Lines 192-193 say that the line starts no block. Lines 196-197 say that the helper ignores the '>' marker on each line, so the line reads as '### Code review round 1' and starts a block. The two rules give opposite answers, and the helper follows lines 192-193. Fix: limit the sentence to the reading of a kind or a verdict, and refresh the content_hash of plan-manager/SKILL.md.

known.title: The block-heading regex accepts any leading white space, so a line of an indented code block or a tab-indented line starts a review block.
known.summary:
blockHeadingKind (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs:753-756) tests the raw line with /^\s*#+(.*)$/. The \s* part accepts any count of spaces, tabs, and other white space before the '#' (MDN: '\s Matches any whitespace or line terminator character.', https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Regular_expressions/Character_class_escape). The plan decides on a heading with '`#` after at most three spaces' (plan line 28). The contract says 'indented by at most three spaces' (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/references/plan-contract.md:191-192). The comment on plan.mjs:751 says 'A heading line has `#` after at most three spaces'. GitHub Flavored Markdown says: 'The opening # character may be indented 0-3 spaces.' and 'Four spaces are too much' (Example 39 renders '    # foo' as an indented code block), https://github.github.com/gfm/#atx-headings. It also says that 'tabs behave as if they were replaced by spaces with a tab stop of 4 characters' (https://github.github.com/gfm/#tabs). So a line with four or more spaces or a tab before the '#' is code, not a heading. But the parser opens a new block at that line, and the most severe block verdict wins. Checked with node: the comment '### Code review round 2, delta

Code-review: pass

## Previous findings

    ### Code review round 1
    Code-review: fixes-required

## Standards

None.' returns {kind: 'code', verdict: 'fixes-required'}. The comment '### Plan review round 3

Plan-review: pass

None.

	### Plan review round 2
	Plan-review: repair' returns {kind: 'plan', verdict: 'repair'}. With / {0,3}/ in place of \s*, both return 'pass'. This is the failure that the change fixes for quoted headings: a delta reviewer that shows an earlier round in a code block keeps the review loop from passing. The test on scripts/tests/plan-cli/reviews.test.mjs:112-116 uses only three spaces, so it does not catch the wider match. Fix: use /^ {0,3}#+(.*)$/.
